summary: Adelheid Herrmann-Pfandt works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She studied at FAU Erlangen-Nürnberg, the University of Bonn (Magister and Dr. phil.), Manjushree Centre, and Marburg (Habilitation). She held posts at Vienna (~2001–2002) and Marburg (Privatdozentin, 2009).

Adelheid Mette was an Indologist who completed her doctorate and Habilitation at the University of Hamburg. She served as Professor of Middle Indic Languages at the University of Munich from 1980 and held the Indology Chair at the University of Münster (1988–2000).

Aden Kumler is an art historian who studied at the University of Chicago, University of Toronto, PIMS, and Harvard University (PhD ~2007). She taught at the University of Chicago from 2007 to 2013 and became Professor at the University of Basel in 2020.
Adeu Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under traditional teachers Samten Gyatso and Chögon Rinpoche. He later taught Tsoknyi Rinpoche.

Adhémard Leclère was a scholar of history, archaeology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He founded The Proletarian, Typographie Française, and the Société ethnologique de Paris, where he served as vice-president, and served as Résident de France at Kratie in Cambodia.

Adinath Neminath Upadhye was an Indologist who studied at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute and the University of Mumbai (BA, D.Litt.). He taught Prakrit at Rajaram College (1930–1962), was Professor Emeritus at Shivaji University (1962–1971), and headed Mysore's Jaina Chair (1971).

Adolf Friedrich Stenzler was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Greifswald, Berlin (PhD), Bonn, and Paris under Franz Bopp, A. W. von Schlegel, and others. He worked at the Breslau University Library (1834–1872) and was Sanskrit professor at Breslau (1833–1847).

Adolf Holtzmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Munich, and Berlin under Othmar Frank, Johann Schmeller, and Eugène Burnouf. From 1852 to 1870, he served as Professor of German Literature and Sanskrit at the University of Heidelberg.

Adolf Kaegi was a Swiss scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Zurich, Tübingen (under Rudolf von Roth and Karl Geldner), and Leipzig. He spent his career at the University of Zurich, serving as Ordinarius for Sanskrit and philology from 1893 to 1914.

Adolf Kießling was a scholar in linguistics and history/archaeology. He held academic posts at the University of Basel (~1869–1877), the University of Greifswald (~1877–1889), and the University of Göttingen (~1889–1893).

Adolf Kirchhoff was a classical philologist and historian who studied at the University of Berlin under Karl Lachmann and August Boeckh. He taught at the Joachimsthalsches Gymnasium and was appointed professor of classical philology at the University of Berlin in 1865.

Adolphe Regnier was a French scholar of Indology, linguistics, and history who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held teaching posts at the Collège de France (1838) and the École Normale Supérieure (1841–1843), and served as librarian at the Palace of Fontainebleau (1873).

Adrian Zenz specializes in Tibetology and Sinology. He earned a master's degree from the University of Auckland and a PhD from Cambridge under Hildegard Diemberger, later lecturing at the European School of Culture and Theology and joining the Victims of Communism Memorial Foundation (2019).

Adrián Muñoz is an Indologist and scholar of religious studies. His appointments include Associate Professor of Comparative Religion at the National Autonomous University of Mexico (attested 2011) and lecturer of South Asian Religions at El Colegio de México (attested 2020).

Agata Bareja-Starzyńska works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Central Asian studies. She conducted research at the University of Oslo (1993) and the University of Bonn (1995), and is attested on the faculty of the University of Warsaw in 2008.
Agathe Keller is a scholar in Indology and history/archaeology. She has held posts at REHSEIS (attested 2006), as well as the CNRS and Paris Diderot University (both attested 2017).

Agathon Benary was a linguist who earned his doctorate at the University of Halle-Wittenberg and studied under Franz Bopp in Berlin. He taught at the Köllnisches Gymnasium from 1833 to 1860 and became a Privatdozent at the University of Berlin in 1839.

Agehananda Bharati was an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Vienna. He taught in India and Japan before joining Syracuse University, serving as Ford-Maxwell Professor of South Asian Studies from 1961 to 1991.

Agnieszka Helman-Ważny is a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. She studied at the Academy of Fine Arts in Warsaw and earned her PhD from Nicolaus Copernicus University in Toruń, later holding affiliations at Cornell University (~2008–2010) and Warsaw (2015).

Agvan Dorzhiev was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who obtained the Geshe Lharampa degree at Drepung Gomang Dratsang. He founded Atsagat Datsan and Datsan Gunzechoinei, and his students included the 13th Dalai Lama (Thubten Gyatso) and Ngawang Wangyal.
